chapter: Faith, Paris life and later years
title: Confronting a Frenchman beating Arab children in Tunis
summary: Clarke seized the stick of a Frenchman beating children on the street and threatened him, to Moody's alarm.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. So I went and -- well, went to walk around Tunis a little bit. So as we were going into the hall to eat, you know, there were some little Arab kids on the street, and this Frenchman had a stick, beating them. So I snatched the stick out of his hand, and I said, 'I'll beat you with this stick if you hit the kid again.' And he said, 'Oh, stay out of it.' I said, 'I won't stay out of anything. Now, you don't beat him anymore or I'm going to beat you good.' He said, 'Oh, you're crazy. Vous etes fou.' I said, 'Yeah? Okay, you hit him again and you'll see who's fou.' So he left. So I said -- and the little kids, they came and grabbed me by the leg and they were kissing my hand, you know. So those were the kind of people who came to France.
Yeah. Yeah. That's too bad, isn't it.
But it just touched me. It touched me like I couldn't believe it.
I said why is he beating those kids?
He said, "Get out of my way."
And Moody said, "Klook, watch it man."
I said, "Man, I don't care what happens." You know, but he's wrong. You know?
: And human, members of the human race.
Yeah. I said when my kid was 10 or 12 years old if somebody beat him I'd kill him.
